questions.question: Under `set -euo pipefail`, what happens when the script reaches `false | true`?
options: Nothing; the pipeline succeeds because true runs last
The script exits, because pipefail makes the pipeline fail if any command in it fails
Bash prints a warning but continues
Only the true command is skipped
questions.explanation: Without pipefail only the last command's status counts. With pipefail the pipeline returns the failing status, and -e then stops the script.

questions.question: In a strict-mode script, why does `local out=$(false)` NOT stop the script?
options: Command substitution is never checked by set -e
local is a builtin that ignores set -u
The exit status of the line is that of `local`, which succeeds, masking the failure
questions.explanation: The status of `local out=$(false)` is the status of the local builtin (0). Declare first (`local out`) and assign on a separate line so the failure is seen.

questions.question: Which trap is the right place to delete a temporary directory so it is removed on both success and failure?
questions.explanation: The EXIT trap fires whenever the script exits, whether it finished normally or was stopped by an error, so it suits cleanup.

questions.question: In `getopts ":vk:d:" opt`, what does the colon after `k` mean?
options: Option -k requires a value, available in $OPTARG
Option -k can be given only once
questions.explanation: A colon after a letter means the option takes an argument, stored in OPTARG. The leading colon of the whole string is what enables silent error handling.
